title: Quality Gates: Phase Advancement Criteria and Gate Failure Behavior
body:
Quality gates prevent incomplete or defective work from advancing through the pipeline. A gate is a binary pass/fail check — if the gate criteria are not met, the phase is not done. Gates serve both agents (who must know when they can advance) and human reviewers (who must know what was verified).

**Gate Model — Five Categories Every Gate Evaluates:**
1. Required outputs exist and are valid — the deliverable is present, complete, and conforms to its schema.
2. Required schemas are populated correctly — no required fields are empty, null, or placeholder-filled.
3. No doctrine violations — the output does not violate any rule in EDITORIAL_DOCTRINE.md.
4. No unresolved blockers — all blockers affecting the current phase are resolved or formally classified and routed.
5. QA perspectives applied where required — phases requiring specific QA reviews have received them.

**Discovery Gate:** Pass condition: a human can read the discovery report and know exactly what will be produced at the next phase, why those choices were made, and what uncertainties remain. No item says 'TBD' without a corresponding blocker entry. Fail condition: any required field is empty; any inferred assumption has no justification; any blocker is undocumented; next actions are vague.

**Brief Gate:** Pass condition: an agent that has never interacted with the user can read only the brief and produce a structurally correct outline without asking questions. The brief is self-contained. Fail condition: any required field is absent or vague; audience is described too broadly; scope boundaries are implicit; success criteria are not testable.

**Outline Gate:** Pass condition: an agent assigned any single section can read the outline and know what to write, what not to write, and what depth to aim for — without asking questions. Fail condition: any section lacks a purpose statement; purpose statements overlap between sections; section order has no stated rationale; a scope area from the brief has no corresponding section.

**Draft Gate:** Pass condition: the draft is ready for merge normalization and QA. A QA agent can evaluate it against defined criteria without making allowances for obvious incompleteness. Fail condition: any section is a placeholder; any section contradicts its outline purpose statement; voice inconsistencies are present but not flagged; citations are claimed but not grounded.

**QA Gate:** Required minimum perspectives: qa-reader, qa-skeptic, qa-coherence, qa-ai-stink. Every issue must be classified as block / revise / note. Issues must be specific — naming the location and the specific problem. Pass condition: no block issues remain unresolved; all revise and note issues are documented and either resolved or formally deferred. Fail condition: any block issue is unresolved; any QA perspective was skipped without authorization; any issue list is a prose summary rather than a structured list.

**Final Gate:** Pass condition: all prior gates passed; voice pass completed; compression pass completed; all doc-level anti-patterns checked and resolved; run log is complete with all phases, decisions, gate results, and override decisions documented. The human reviewer's job is judgment, not cleanup.

**Gate Failure Behavior:** List exactly which criteria are unmet. Return to the appropriate stage. Do not advance to the next phase under any circumstances. Document the gate failure in the run cache.

**Override Rule:** Any gate may be explicitly overridden by the user. The override must be requested explicitly, logged with reason and scope in the run cache, and scoped to the current run. Silent gate bypass is never permitted.
